artworks.title: Dites donc, M'sieu Colimard ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of four individuals engaged in reading and discussing newspapers or documents in an interior setting. The drawing shows a group gathered around a table, where two people are seated and focused on the papers in front of them. One figure leans on the desk, while another stands in the background reading a document. The setting suggests a room for reading or news exchange, with drawings and notes scattered across the table. The characters have detailed expressions, contributing to the contemplative atmosphere of the scene.

artworks.title: Un Décembrisé
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image features a person standing with their arms crossed, facing another figure in the background. The person has distinctive facial features, wears a headscarf, and a patterned garment. They stand next to an open doorway where a second person is leaning on a railing. The background shows interior walls and door frames.

artworks.title: Les suites d'une discussion politique ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image showcases two full-body caricatures of men in a black and white scene. The man on the left is depicted in an exaggerated pose with one foot forward and arms raised upward. He has balding hair with curly hair remaining, deep lines defining his facial features, and wears a long coat, white shirt, and trousers. The man on the right stands with arms crossed, wearing a neutral expression. He is bald with a prominent nose and chin, dressed in a snug dark suit. Both characters are set against a background with tent-like shapes, with no additional objects or details present.

artworks.title: Une séance du conseil des cinq
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts five men at a table engaging in conversation. They are dressed in formal 18th or early 19th-century attire. Four men are seated in various poses, while one man stands. The setting is simple with a plain wall in the background.

artworks.title: Je vous dis que ... il nous faut M. Molé ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two men engaged in conversation. The drawing captures two figures seated outdoors, surrounded by foliage, with one figure seated on a rustic chair and the other more informally perched on what appears to be a rock or a low wall. The person on the left seems to be listening intently with a contemplative expression, while the person on the right appears animated, gesturing with their mouth open as if speaking. The setting is informal and natural, possibly taking place in a garden or park. The text at the bottom adds an element of dialogue. The depiction evokes a sense of leisurely discussion amidst a serene natural backdrop.

artworks.title: Frappez et on vous ouvrira!
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a figure humorously trying to access a building named "Académie Française." The figure is depicted with a tall hat and a playful expression, knocking on a door labeled with the institution's name while holding a book or satchel. The phrase "Frappez et on vous ouvrira!" (translated as "Knock and it shall be opened to you!") is included. The lines and shading techniques give a satirical tone to the illustration.

artworks.title: Rentrée des Capucins dans ... Paris
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of capuchin monks encountering two comical figures at a gate. The image depicts four monks approaching a gate guarded by two unusual gatekeepers. One of the gatekeepers wears a conical hat with a tassel and both peer over a tall religious newspaper labeled "UNIVER RELIGIEUX." A sign on the gate reads "BARRIÈRE D'ENFER ROUTE DE MONTROUGE." The monks exhibit expressions of curiosity. This is in the style of Honoré Daumier.

artworks.title: Les burgraves allant en guerre
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of soldiers advancing towards a symbolic structure labeled "Suffrage Universel." The image features four caricatured figures with large heads and exaggerated costumes, marching with determination. They are wielding spears and flags, heading towards a hill where the symbolic structure stands. The medium appears to be pen and ink with detailed cross-hatching and shading. The drawing has a satirical and playful tone.

artworks.title: Un autodafé au XIXe  siècle
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a person in a conical hat performing an action at a fire. The drawing depicts a figure with a long robe and a conical hat, kneeling at a fire made of books and fanning the flames. In the background, there are three large statues or figures with conical hats labeled "EURIPIDE," "MOLIÈRE," and "SOPHOCLE." The setting appears to allude to a ceremonial or ritualistic act, emphasized by the exaggerated smoke and stylized robes and hats. The title at the bottom suggests a commentary on acts of censorship or cultural suppression, echoed by the burning of books. The use of shading and lines gives a detailed and expressive feel to the composition.

artworks.title: Allant aux renseignements politiques ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring two figures engaging in conversation at a doorway. One figure wears a bonnet and shawl marked "OPINION PUBLIQUE," while the other is dressed formally with a top hat labeled "L'ORDRE." The person inside the doorway gestures with their hands. The scene appears satirical and may critique political or social themes.

artworks.title: Vue prise au Père Lachaise
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is an image of two figures mourning in front of a tombstone. The tombstone is inscribed with "CI-GIT LE COMITÉ DE LA RUE DE POITIERS CONCESSION A PERPÉTUITÉ" and topped with an urn labeled "SCRUTIN DU 10 MARS." One figure wears a top hat and rests against a sack labeled "LA PATRIE," while the other figure has a head covering and leans against a bundle marked "LE CONST. TUTUMEL." The scene is drawn in a monochromatic, sketchy style, reminiscent of Honoré Daumier.

artworks.title: Les moucherons politiques
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is an image of anthropomorphized insects surrounding a candle. The flies have human-like faces and are depicted with exaggerated facial expressions. They are arranged in a circle around the lit candle, some insects are numbered. Other insects below the candle appear lifeless or tired. The background and style suggest a political or social theme.

artworks.title: Les nouveaux Icares
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of multiple figures falling from the sky. The figures have exaggerated facial features and limbs flailing as they descend. Feathers fill the background and sunlight beams down. The drawing conveys a sense of chaos and impending doom. The sketch uses framing, shadows, and detailed drawing to create a satirical tone.

artworks.title: Les Parisiens ayant trouvé le moyen de circuler ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring a flooded street scene with individuals navigating the water using stilts. The artwork shows people in period clothing with top hats and dresses walking on stilts above the water level. In the background, there are trees and indistinct figures. The style is reminiscent of Honoré Daumier's satirical illustrations of societal norms.

artworks.title: Prestation ... d'un ... membre ... du dix Décembre ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows three men depicted from foot to shoulder height. The man on the left is leaning forward, with his mouth open and holding a glass. He has exaggerated facial features, including a prominent nose and chin, and wears a cap with short hair visible beneath it. He is dressed in a loose-fitting garment with vertical stripes on his trousers. The central figure stands upright with one arm casually extended and is depicted in partial profile. He wears a tall top hat, a large mustache, and sideburns, dressed in a long coat and striped trousers. He holds a glass in one hand and a large club in the other. The man on the right, who is also partly in profile, has a long, narrow face and a full beard. He wears a cap and loose shirt with rolled sleeves, holding a club similar to the central figure's. His trousers are tucked at the ankles, and he is depicted with an open stance. The background features faces of several other figures holding glasses with indistinct features. The drawing includes cross-hatching and scribbles in the background. The overall tone is monochromatic, with stark lines and heavy shading.

artworks.title: On dit que les jolies femmes sont ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows two women standing side by side. The woman on the left has her arms crossed, while the woman on the right is holding a cane or long stick in front of her. The woman on the left has a rounded face with distinct features and dark hair in a bun, wearing a long dress. The woman on the right has a surprised or concerned expression, with wide eyes and a slightly open mouth, her hair covered with a bonnet and wearing a long dress and shawl. The background includes a simple interior with a sketch of a door, sparse wall lines, and a framed picture hanging on the wall.

artworks.title: Molé apportant des étrennes au petit thiers
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two caricatured figures, one presenting a jack-in-the-box to the other. The first figure is on the left bending over, extending the toy to the second figure on the right. The jack-in-the-box has an animated head with enlarged eyes and a wide grin. The second figure seems surprised by the toy. The style of the drawing includes bold lines and exaggerated proportions.

artworks.title: Le sauvage bineau ayant ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a caricature of a figure with exaggerated features and a large club causing chaos in a public setting. The figure has an elongated head and small stature, swinging a club while running. There is an inscription "PROJET DE LOI PUBLIQUE" on their back. The background includes trees, buildings, and chaos, possibly in a city boulevard. The style is reminiscent of editorial cartoons or satirical depictions from the 19th century, using expressive line work and exaggerated forms.

artworks.title: Un réconciliation, scène de haute comédie ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two individuals embracing, both with serious expressions. The central figures have exaggerated features and wear formal attire. They look in opposite directions with their arms around each other. In the background, other figures watch. The style and features suggest the work of a caricaturist. The text at the bottom indicates a satirical or humorous intent, depicting feigned reconciliation.

artworks.title: L'Hercule des Champs-Elysées
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a muscular figure holding a large club. The figure is on the right side, with exaggerated muscles and shorts. They have an intense expression. On the left side, there is a smaller figure in motion. The drawing includes two blocks labeled "PROROGATION" and "PRIVISION." In the background, there is a faint structure resembling the Arc de Triomphe. The title is "L'hercule des Champs-Élysées." The drawing features caricatured and exaggerated features typical of satirical illustrations.

artworks.title: Une mauvaise cuisine
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of three figures stirring a cauldron filled with papers. The work depicts three figures engaged with a large cauldron overflowing with sheets of paper. Each figure is holding a pole with a sign at the top – the signs read "Le Constitutionnel," "L'Assemblée Nationale," and "La Patrie." The figures have exaggerated facial expressions and movements, indicating activity. The scene symbolizes the mixing of ideas or political turmoil, as suggested by the titles on the signs. The drawing is detailed, capturing the motion and intensity of the scene.

artworks.title: Passez au large!
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a large urn labeled "Suffrage Universel" being guarded by a rotund figure holding a staff, with a crowd looking on from the background.

artworks.title: Aux Champs-Elysées, Ratapoil. Par suite d'une délibération philantropique [sic] du Comité du dix Décembre...à deux sous à club...deux sous...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The drawing features a man with exaggerated facial features wearing a top hat, holding sticks under one arm while another stick points upwards. He is surrounded by indistinct figures in suits and top hats. The background is sketched lightly, indicating a street setting.

artworks.title: Le sire de Berryer ...Chevalier ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two individuals in a caricatured style. One person is kneeling, while the other is standing holding a large stick above the kneeling figure's head. The style features exaggerated features characteristic of caricatures and suggests a contrast between the characters. The scene appears to depict a satirical or ceremonial moment. The linework is bold and distinctive, emphasizing the comical nature of the illustration.
